Subject: PO vs card — procurement & onboarding follow-up

Hi Jamie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps: 

- FinOps goal: centralize LLM spend under procurement; AP requires vendor onboarding for new suppliers.
- Procurement constraints discussed: PO preferred for vendor spend > $25k/year; corporate card OK for pilot < $5k.
- Questions for you:
  1) Does FinOpsCo require a standard vendor packet (W9, insurance, SLA) before issuing a PO?
  2) Is there an internal vendor onboarding portal or form you can share?
  3) Are you open to purchasing via the AWS Marketplace/GC Marketplace (we can provide an AMI/listing) if that speeds procurement?

Proposed next steps:
1) If PO path: send vendor onboarding form and standard PO template — we’ll fill and return within 48 hours.
2) If card path for pilot: we can set up a short-term card billing and move to PO at renewal/expansion.
3) I’ll loop in our finance ops lead (Lauren) to confirm docs and timing.

Attaching a short vendor checklist that usually speeds the onboarding process — happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Marissa

marissa@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

From: Jamie Ortiz <jamie.ortiz@finopsco.com>

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers: 

- Yes, FinOpsCo standard is to issue a PO for recurring vendor spend expected to exceed $25k/year. For small pilots under $5k we typically allow card payment to move faster.
- We do require a W9 and a completed vendor onboarding form (I attached our standard PDF) and a copy of standard SLA/insurance if applicable.
- Marketplace is an interesting option — procurement sometimes prefers marketplace purchases because of simplified billing, though it depends on the finance owner. If you have a Marketplace listing, send details and I’ll flag it to procurement.

I’ve attached our vendor_onboarding_form.pdf and looped in Alex from AP to confirm the timing and any additional fields we need. Ideally we’d have the vendor packet filled out this week so we can get a PO on file before the pilot kickoff.

Best,
Jamie Ortiz
Head of Procurement, FinOpsCo
jamie.ortiz@finopsco.com

Marissa / Jamie — quick note from AP: we can issue a PO once vendor onboarding form and W9 are complete. Typical turnaround is 5–7 business days after we receive complete docs and vendor is entered in our system. For urgent pilots under $5k, we can approve a corporate card payment with a single invoice.

Two items we need from Redwood to add vendor:
- Completed W9 (signed)
- Company payment remittance instructions (bank ACH details) OR indicate if you prefer credit card processing and provide billing contact.

I attached our W9 intake checklist for your reference. Once the vendor profile is created, we’ll provide a vendor code and PO template.

Thanks,
Alex Nguyen
AP Manager, FinOpsCo
